title: Circular Couette (swirl): rigid-rotation patch, Dirichlet- and shear-driven Couette, torque
physics: annulus 1 < r < 2, 0 < z < 1 (no axis), mu = 7/10, do-nothing on z = 0, 1 (holds in both forms); u_theta = r; u_theta = -r/3 + 4/(3r); shear-driven u_theta = 10 r/7 - 10/(7 r)

parameters.formulation: weight r in every volume and boundary integral; continuity tested with r q (symmetric saddle point); grad u with the hoop entries (r,theta) = -u_theta/r, (theta,theta) = u_r/r; lap a = int mu grad u : grad v r, sym a = int 2 mu eps(u) : eps(v) r; traction g = sigma_form n (vector (g_r, g_z, g_theta)); grad-div gamma (div_r u, div_r v)_r with div_r u = d_r u_r + u_r/r + d_z u_z, the weight r, gamma in viscosity units (tools/fluids_mms/axi_stokes.py docstring)

solver.tight: same, plus 2 steps of iterative refinement (vacuous for a direct solve; meaningful for an iterative path)

parameters.axis_rule: Axis r = 0 (attribute 'axis'): u_r = u_theta = 0 STRONGLY at every P2 velocity node on the axis (vertices and edge nodes), rows and columns eliminated (the assembled axis-axis entries are never used); u_z and p natural. No quadrature point on r = 0 (the hoop integrands u v / r are rational on elements that touch the axis at one vertex).
parameters.shared_node_rule: At a velocity node shared by several boundary attributes: (1) Dirichlet beats every natural condition and the axis condition (the fixed data satisfy u_r = u_theta = 0 at r = 0 anyway); (2) between Dirichlet attributes the fixed data AGREE at shared nodes (one exact callable per field: checked by dirichlet_shared_node_mismatch_max), so the result does not depend on attribute order; (3) a node shared by the axis and a natural (traction / do-nothing) attribute takes the axis condition u_r = u_theta = 0 (strong) and the natural condition for u_z.
parameters.dirichlet_data: Dirichlet data by P2 LAGRANGE NODAL INTERPOLATION of the fixed callable (exact at vertices and edge nodes); checked on the solution by dirichlet_nodal_data_defect_max.
parameters.quadrature: QUADRATURE REQUIREMENTS: (a) no quadrature point on r = 0; (b) the viscous rule (including the 1/r hoop terms) and the load rule exact to degree >= 4 on affine elements (the order-4 functionals need it; degree 3 drops the torque orders to 2.96); (c) the continuity / pressure coupling (div_r v, q)_r integrated exactly, i.e. degree >= 3 on affine elements; (d) grad-div assembled with the SAME rule as the viscous 1/r terms. The constant-mu identity and continuity_rq_max_rel hold to round-off only under (c) and (d) (measured: a degree-2 grad-div rule gives identity p 5e-7, a degree-2 (div, q) rule continuity 3e-5).

structured.construction: f1b_stokes_check.annulus_rect_mesh(N) = f1a_stokes_check.structured_mesh(N, x0=1, x1=2) with (x, y) = (r, z); nested

boundaries.r2: dirichlet (rotation, couette) / traction (shear-driven: sigma_form n from the field)

convergence.norm: ||u_theta - u_theta,h||_{L2_r}: the swirl component alone (a swirl-only defect cannot hide in the total)
|u_theta - u_theta,h|_{H1_r} with the hoop term e_t^2/r^2: the swirl component alone
||u_theta - u_theta,h||_{L2_r}: the swirl component alone (a swirl-only defect cannot hide in the total)
|u_theta - u_theta,h|_{H1_r} with the hoop term e_t^2/r^2: the swirl component alone
||u_theta - u_theta,h||_{L2_r}: the swirl component alone (a swirl-only defect cannot hide in the total)
|u_theta - u_theta,h|_{H1_r} with the hoop term e_t^2/r^2: the swirl component alone
||u_theta - u_theta,h||_{L2_r}: the swirl component alone (a swirl-only defect cannot hide in the total)
|u_theta - u_theta,h|_{H1_r} with the hoop term e_t^2/r^2: the swirl component alone

|T_h - T| / |T|: T_h the Babuska-Miller torque of the fluid on the inner cylinder (f1b_stokes_check.reaction, Cauchy stress, w = r e_theta at the inner-wall nodes), T the closed form (per radian; generator: torque_inner_per_radian)

|T_h - T| / |T|: T_h the Babuska-Miller torque of the fluid on the inner cylinder (f1b_stokes_check.reaction, Cauchy stress, w = r e_theta at the inner-wall nodes), T the closed form (per radian; generator: torque_inner_per_radian)
